svg.text: Tang Nano 20K: the 6809 and the SDRAM with the clocks (RTL trace, read cache + posted writes, 54 MHz)
1 clock = 18.5 ns, E cycle = 28 clocks. Code in RAM: jsr $0300 (first time: cache miss), two pushes on the stack (posted writes), then the fetch of $0300 again (hit).
24 clk held: request, ACT, READ (CL 2), data (a refresh came in between)
writes are posted: the CPU is not held,
the controller writes in the background (10 clk each)
SDRAM clock = the system clock inverted (a PLL output 180 degrees off): the controller changes the command at a rising edge of the system clock, the SDRAM takes it half a clock later (dashed lines).
SDRAM command: A = ACTIVE (open the row), R = READ with auto precharge (data 3 clocks later), W = WRITE with auto precharge, F = AUTO REFRESH. An access takes 9-10 clocks, one at a time.
Bus cycle: the number is its length; 28 clocks is the E cycle with no wait; a cache miss makes it 41. A hit (the last $0300 fetch) and a posted write take no extra time.
Measured on the RTL of fpga/tn20k (Verilator, tb.cpp VCD), not on the board. Signals: soc.e, cpu_a, stall, cc_hit, ps_rd/ps_wr, ctl_busy, sd_ras_n/cas_n/we_n.
